fichas.title: Recording and Surveying Existing Buildings
fichas.summary: Existing-building documentation should be undertaken before decisions about construction measures and future use. Site drawings and a room schedule help identify defects and building condition, and provide a basis for design, cost estimation, defect mapping and construction documentation. Investigations should minimize damage; intrusive work should be agreed with the client and historic buildings authority and performed by experts. A room schedule records each room in text and graphics, including necessary measures and completed work.
uses: Support refurbishment planning and cost estimation
Record room information and work undertaken

fichas.title: Measurement Precision Stages for Existing Buildings
fichas.summary: The page presents five stages of recording and measurement, from schematic recording for layout planning and approximate floor-area calculations to exact measurement for demanding archaeology and building research. Drawing scales are shown in the source table but are reproduction scales, not physical dimensions. Stages I and II may be extended up to stage V for difficult historic-building projects and scientific investigations.
uses: Select an appropriate level of building survey precision
Inform restoration, construction drawings and scientific investigation
